name: Oklahoma

sales.rateNote: State rate 4.5% of gross receipts; county and municipal sales taxes are added where the sale is sourced (point of delivery).

local.levies: counties and incorporated cities and towns (voter-approved sales and use taxes)
local.capNote: The general county sales tax under 68 O.S. §1370 may not exceed 2% and needs voter approval; other statutes authorize additional county levies, and municipalities set their own rates, so no single overall cap.

groceries.note: State rate on food and food ingredients is 0% since August 29, 2024 (HB 1955 and SB 1283, 2024); local city and county sales taxes still apply. Prepared food, alcohol and dietary supplements stay taxable at 4.5%.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable except during the August back-to-school holiday (articles under $100).

otherRates.note: Motor vehicle excise tax of 3.25% of value on new vehicles, plus a 1.25% portion of state sales tax; vehicles are not subject to city or county sales taxes.

holidays2026.name: Back-to-school sales tax holiday
holidays2026.items: articles of clothing or footwear priced under $100 (not athletic/protective gear, accessories or rentals)

sales.holidayNote: Dates follow 68 O.S. §1357.10 (first Friday in August through the following Sunday); the holiday exempts the state 4.5% portion only.

useTax.note: State use tax of 4.5% on goods brought into Oklahoma untaxed, plus any county or city use tax.

facts.text: Since August 29, 2024 grocery food carries a 0% state sales tax, but local sales taxes still apply to it.
Rotisserie chicken, deli sandwiches, fountain drinks, pet food, vitamins and over-the-counter medicine remain taxable at the 4.5% state rate.
A seller whose prepared-food sales exceed 75% of food sales and who makes utensils available must charge state tax on all its food items.
A general county sales tax may not exceed 2% and must first be approved by county voters.
Veterans with a 100% service-connected disability can get a sales tax exemption permit covering up to $25,000 of purchases per year.
Retailers must still compute sales tax to the cent even if cash totals are rounded to the nickel after the end of penny production.

property.levied: local only (ad valorem): counties, school districts, cities and other local districts; assessed by county assessors, with the Oklahoma Tax Commission valuing public service property

assessment.text: Real property is assessed at a county-set percentage of fair cash value between 11% and 13.5% (State Board of Equalization range). The fair cash value of homestead and agricultural land may not rise more than 3% a year (5% for other property) unless the property is sold or improved (Okla. Const. art. X §8B).
assessment.capText: Real property is assessed at a county-set percentage of fair cash value between 11% and 13.5% (State Board of Equalization range). The fair cash value of homestead and agricultural land may not rise more than 3% a year (5% for other property) unless the property is sold or improved (Okla. Const. art. X §8B).

homestead.name: Homestead Exemption
homestead.text: Each owner-occupied homestead is exempt from all ad valorem taxes on $1,000 of assessed value (68 O.S. §2889). An additional $1,000 of assessed value is exempt for heads of household with gross household income of $30,000 or less (68 O.S. §2890).
homestead.applyBy: Apply to the county assessor (OTC Form 921) on or before March 15, or within 30 days of a notice of valuation increase; no need to reapply while you keep living there.

otherRelief.name: Senior valuation limitation (freeze)
otherRelief.text: Homeowners 65+ whose gross household income is at or below the HUD-based limit for their county (e.g. $99,000 in Cleveland County for 2026) can have their home's value frozen.

otherRelief.name: Additional homestead exemption
otherRelief.text: Extra $1,000 of assessed value exempt when household income is $30,000 or less; applied for on OTC Form 994 by March 15.

otherRelief.name: 100% disabled veteran exemption
otherRelief.text: Full exemption of the homestead's fair cash value for veterans rated 100% permanently disabled by the VA, extending to the surviving spouse (OTC Form 998).

dueDates.text: Taxes are due November 1. If at least half is paid before January 1, the remainder is due before April 1; otherwise the whole bill is delinquent January 1. Delinquent taxes bear 1.5% interest per month.

facts.text: State Board of Equalization sets the assessment level at 11%-13.5% of fair cash value for real property and 10%-15% for personal property.
Fair cash value of homesteads and farmland cannot rise more than 3% per year, other property 5%, except after a sale or improvement.
Bills of $25 or less must be paid in full before January 1; installments are capped at two.
Homestead exemption is cancelled if the owner has delinquent personal property taxes on the county lien docket.
Public service property is valued by the OTC: 11.84% for railroads and airlines, 12% for video service providers and 22.85% for other public service companies.
